A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AdaCtrl research. All pages, equations, tables, and figures support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-training and evaluation results, including accuracy, response lengths, controllability experiments, and training dynamics.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds 14B experiments, hyperparameter sweeps, reward ablations, and further analyses.

M1.justification: The two-stage training procedure, Easy/Hard control interface, rollout-based difficulty estimation, three reward components, and GRPO objective remain unchanged. The 14B experiments extend model-size settings without introducing a new algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: DeepMATH training and evaluation on AIME2024, AIME2025, MATH500, and GSM8K are retained. The additional experiments vary model size, rewards, and prompting within the existing mathematical task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds the evaluated S1.1-7B-PE prompting baseline in Figure 4(b), reporting response lengths under a requested 500-token limit. The existing comparison methods remain, with renamed rows and corresponding 14B configurations.

E3.justification: V2 adds matched 14B training/evaluation, reward-removal experiments, reward-weight combinations, and difficulty-threshold sweeps over 0.625, 0.5, and 0.375. It also tests prompted 500-token limits and qualitatively reports a 1000-token test. Previously stated data budgets, metrics, and decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds individual reward ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity tests, comparison with prompted length control, and response-length distributions by predicted difficulty. It also expands final difficulty-tag proportions into trajectories during RL, directly examining how difficulty judgments develop.

E5.justification: Both versions average AIME2024 and AIME2025 performance over eight independent runs. V2 adds no seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: The original 7B results in Tables 1–2 remain unchanged. V2 adds extensive results under new conditions: AdaCtrl-14B achieves 34.58% accuracy with 15173.21 tokens on AIME2024, while 7B reward ablations yield 17.08% without calibration reward and 15.42% without length reward. Hyperparameter, prompting, and distribution analyses add further findings; these are additional results rather than same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain their mathematical substance. Renaming reasoning traces from r to p and distinguishing the KL coefficient as beta-prime are notation refinements. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims of adaptive budgeting, explicit user control, and difficulty-aware two-stage training are retained. V2 additionally claims robustness under hyperparameter variation in the introduction; its abstract and conclusion otherwise preserve the original contribution scope.

C2.justification: V2 adds localized interpretations: initial Easy-tag bias is attributed primarily to format learning during SFT, prompting failures are linked to instruction-following limitations, and binary difficulty categories are justified by control simplicity and reliability. It also interprets the new ablations and sweeps as supporting reward complementarity and robustness.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies the default difficulty threshold as 0.625 and supplies exact baseline and difficulty-aware evaluation prompts in Section 4.1. These disclosures do not establish changes to the existing experiments. Software, hardware, optimizer details, and the promised future code release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Wei et al.'s chain-of-thought work and two Hongru Wang et al. papers, while removing the ThinkPrune citation. The introduction more explicitly contrasts uniform compression with brittle fine-grained prompting. Most related-work discussion and the overall novelty positioning remain intact; duplicate-reference consolidation does not remove those works.

P1.justification: The introduction and substantial portions of the method/results narrative are rewritten. The separate tag-interface subsection is integrated into cold-start training, RL subsections are consolidated, and controllability moves from analysis into main results. Terminology shifts from length-trigger tags to difficulty-aware tags.

P2.justification: V2 removes the opening summary chart, redesigns the retained example and training diagrams, expands Tables 1–2, and adds Tables 3–4. Final tag-proportion bars become training trajectories, with new prompting and distribution plots. The retained training curves also change their step-axis scale from 0–640 to 0–80 without explanation.

improvement.justification: V1 lacked individual reward ablations and sensitivity tests and evaluated only a 7B backbone. V2 substantially strengthens validation through separate reward-removal controls, threshold/weight sweeps, and matched 14B comparisons, while disclosing previously missing prompts and the default threshold. Reporting weaknesses remain: some mode-comparison claims overgeneralize Table 2, and the training-step axis changes unexplained. These issues limit precision but do not outweigh the substantial gains in testing the method's components and robustness.
